taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-29, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 995.1 | 4.02 | 4.02
2 | 1300.6 | 35.56 | 39.58
3 | 381.3 | 12.04 | 51.62
4 | 1563.6 | 22.76 | 74.38
5 | 1611.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-29, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-29 in Survey Area T consists of five resistivity layers. The sequence begins with a resistivity of 995.1 $\Omega\cdot$m, increasing to 1300.6 $\Omega\cdot$m in the second layer. This is followed by a significant decrease to 381.3 $\Omega\cdot$m in the third layer, and a subsequent rise through the fourth (1563.6 $\Omega\cdot$m) and fifth (1611.9 $\Omega\cdot$m) layers. Applying the VES curve-type notation for these layers, the sequence is K-H-A. The existing file classification of KHA-type is accurate and consistent with the interpreted layer model.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
